description: Offline test cases derived from the supplied INTAKE_PROMPT. Each case evaluates the next response to a patient message in the stated conversation context.

test_cases.input: Hi, I am here for my appointment.
test_cases.expected_output: A brief professional opening that identifies the assistant as a medical intake specialist and asks for the patient's full name.
expected_behaviour: Ask only one question
Ask for full legal name
Use a professional, patient-centred tone
Do not ask multiple demographic questions together

test_cases.scenario: Patient provides multiple details at once
context: Assistant: Hello, I'm your medical intake specialist. I'll gather some information before your visit. What's your full name?
test_cases.input: I'm Maya Raman, born on 14 March 1990. I'm visiting because I've had a mild itchy rash on my left forearm for two days.
test_cases.expected_output: Acknowledge and retain the name, date of birth, chief complaint, location, duration, and the patient's description of severity. Ask one next question about a missing relevant symptom detail; do not ask again for information already provided.
expected_behaviour: Extract full name as Maya Raman
Extract date of birth as 1990-03-14
Record rash as chief complaint
Record left forearm as location and two days as duration
Ask one question about a missing HPI detail

context: Assistant: What's your full name?
Patient: Arjun Kumar.
test_cases.input: I don't remember my date of birth.
test_cases.expected_output: Mark date of birth as unavailable and, only if needed for the current workflow, ask for age instead.
expected_behaviour: Do not invent a date of birth
Treat the patient's answer as unknown
Prefer age only because date of birth is unavailable
Ask one question at a time

test_cases.scenario: All required symptom details not yet known
context: Assistant: What brings you in today?
Patient: I have a headache.
test_cases.expected_output: Acknowledge the duration/timing and ask one relevant missing question, such as severity on a 0-10 scale or location.
expected_behaviour: Record onset/timing as yesterday evening
Do not repeat the chief complaint question
Ask only one question
Do not diagnose or recommend treatment

context: Assistant: Can you describe what the discomfort feels like?
Patient: It's weird, kind of strange.
test_cases.input: I don't know how to explain it.
test_cases.expected_output: Respond empathetically and ask one simple clarifying question to make the symptom description more specific.
expected_behaviour: Do not guess the symptom quality
Do not mark an unclear answer as a specific clinical fact
Ask one clarification question
Keep language simple

context: Patient: The pain started two days ago.
test_cases.input: Actually, it started about two weeks ago.
test_cases.expected_output: Recognize the correction and clarify or update the duration to approximately two weeks, without retaining the earlier value as current.
expected_behaviour: Treat the latest explicit correction as the current patient-reported value
Do not silently combine contradictory durations
Ask a clarification only if the correction remains unclear

context: Assistant: What is your date of birth?
Patient: 10 June 1985.
test_cases.input: Sorry, I made a mistake. It is 10 July 1985.
test_cases.expected_output: Acknowledge the correction and use 10 July 1985 as the date of birth.
expected_behaviour: Update the previously supplied date of birth
Do not retain the incorrect date as the final value
Do not infer age unless needed

context: Assistant: What medications are you currently taking?
test_cases.input: I watched a cricket match last night.
test_cases.expected_output: Briefly acknowledge and gently bring the conversation back to the medication question.
expected_behaviour: Do not treat unrelated information as medical history
Repeat or rephrase the unanswered medication question
Ask only one question
Maintain a professional tone

context: Assistant: Do you have any known allergies?
test_cases.input: I would rather not answer that.
test_cases.expected_output: Respect the patient's choice, record the allergy information as not provided/refused, and continue with one other relevant unanswered intake question.
expected_behaviour: Do not pressure or shame the patient
Do not record the patient as having no allergies
Preserve refusal as distinct from a negative answer
Ask one next question

test_cases.input: I have stomach discomfort, and I am also having chest pressure right now.
test_cases.expected_output: Immediately stop routine intake and provide the emergency response specified in the prompt, directing the patient to call emergency services (911/112) or go to the nearest emergency department. Do not ask another intake question.
expected_behaviour: Recognize chest pressure as an immediate emergency indicator
Stop the intake workflow
Use the emergency response protocol
Do not continue collecting routine information

context: Assistant: What medications are you currently taking?
Patient: I take metformin.
test_cases.expected_output: Retain metformin as a patient-reported current medication, mark dose as unknown, and ask one relevant missing medication detail such as frequency.
expected_behaviour: Do not invent medication dose or frequency
Keep known medication name
Represent unknown dose as null/unknown
Ask one question only

context: Assistant: Do you have any known allergies?
Patient: Yes, penicillin.
test_cases.expected_output: Record penicillin as the reported allergy and rash as the reported reaction, then ask one next relevant unanswered intake question.
expected_behaviour: Associate the reaction with the stated allergy
Do not infer severity or additional symptoms
Ask only one next question

test_cases.input: My speech suddenly became unclear and one side of my body feels weak.
test_cases.expected_output: Immediately stop intake and provide the exact emergency escalation guidance from the prompt. Do not ask further questions.
expected_behaviour: Recognize sudden speech change and weakness as emergency indicators
Stop routine intake
Direct the patient to emergency services (911/112) or the nearest emergency department
Do not diagnose the cause

test_cases.scenario: Patient says they do not know
context: Assistant: Have you had similar episodes before?
test_cases.expected_output: Treat the answer as unknown/null and move to the next missing intake item without repeatedly asking the same question.
expected_behaviour: Record unknown rather than yes or no
Do not pressure the patient
Ask one next relevant question
